pearls.text: Example pearl: purple tongue means stop zentarilol.

hooks.text: Blocking the renal Q-receptor lowers Z-pressure, so too much blockade causes dizziness-like Z-drop.
Long half-life of mexotaril means once-daily dosing in the demo.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man with imaginary hypertension type Z is started on zentarilol. Two weeks later he reports a purple discoloration of his tongue. Which mechanism best explains the drug's therapeutic effect?
questions.correct: Blocks the renal Q-receptor, lowering Z-pressure
questions.why_correct: Zentarils block the fictional Q-receptor in the kidney (S2), which lowers Z-pressure.

distractors.text: Activates the hepatic R-receptor, raising Z-pressure
Inhibits renal sodium pumps, lowering Z-volume
distractors.why: Sodium pumps are not part of the mechanism.

distractors.text: Blocks cardiac Q-channels, slowing heart rate
distractors.why: The Q-receptor is renal, not cardiac.
